correctness.rationale: For strictly positive real additive valuations of two agents on a path, the actual proof distinguishes global Pareto dominance by all allocations from dominance restricted to connected allocations. At m<=2 singleton splits yield EF1 and one undominated split; at m=3 eight utility vectors are compared in five exhaustive cases after normalizing a>=c by path reversal. The strict inequalities rule out simultaneous domination of all EF1 candidates. For m=4, v1=(1,1,1,1), v2=(1,2,2,1): each one/three connected split fails EF1, each two/two cut has (2,3) strictly Pareto-dominated by disconnected endpoint/middle allocation (2,4), and all-to-one fails EF1. Chore transfer exchanges bundles and complements each cost, conserving connectivity, EF1 and Pareto dominance. Independent exhaustive positive integer search of 819 profiles for n=1,2,3 with weights 1..3 and exact four-item witness reproduced this; enumeration is not the proof for arbitrary reals.

The specific sharp four-positive-additive-item obstruction, including the m<=3 universal lower bound and chores dual, is not implied by the inspected earlier theorems.
